examples.question_text: A vertical mast has top $T$ and foot $O$. A cable from ground point $A$ to $T$ is $26\text{ m}$ long and makes an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with level ground. Ground point $B$ is $20\text{ m}$ from $O$. Find the angle of elevation $\theta$ of $T$ from $B$, correct to 1 decimal place.

A vertical lighthouse $OT$ is $40\text{ m}$ high. Boats $P$ and $Q$ are on bearings of $030^{\circ}\text{T}$ and $120^{\circ}\text{T}$ respectively from its foot $O$. The angles of depression from $T$ to $P$ and $Q$ are $45^{\circ}$ and $30^{\circ}$ respectively. Find the distance between the boats in exact form.

A rectangular prism has base $ABCD$, with $AB=9\text{ cm}$ and $BC=12\text{ cm}$. Vertex $G$ is directly above $C$, with $CG=7\text{ cm}$. Find the angle $\theta$ that space diagonal $AG$ makes with the base, correct to the nearest degree.

A right square pyramid has base $ABCD$ of side length $20\text{ cm}$. Its apex $T$ is directly above the base centre $O$, and $OT=14\text{ cm}$. Point $M$ is the midpoint of $AB$. Find the angle between face $TAB$ and the base, correct to 1 decimal place.

A right square pyramid has base $ABCD$ of side length $12\text{ cm}$. Its apex $V$ is directly above the base centre $O$, and slant edge $VA=12\text{ cm}$. Find the exact angle $\alpha$ that $VA$ makes with the base.

A vertical tower has foot $F$ and top $T$. Point $P$ is due south of $F$, and point $Q$ is due east of $F$, on level ground. The angles of elevation of $T$ from $P$ and $Q$ are $30^{\circ}$ and $45^{\circ}$ respectively. If $PQ=100\text{ m}$, find the exact height $h$ of the tower.

A tower with foot $F$ and top $T$ stands due north of ground point $A$. A surveyor walks $60\text{ m}$ due east from $A$ to $B$. The angles of elevation of $T$ from $A$ and $B$ are $45^{\circ}$ and $30^{\circ}$ respectively. Find the tower height $h$, correct to 1 decimal place.

A tower has foot $O$ and top $T$. It is due north of observer $A$ and due west of observer $B$. The observers are $80\text{ m}$ apart, and the bearing of $B$ from $A$ is $060^{\circ}\text{T}$. The angle of elevation of $T$ from $A$ is $30^{\circ}$. Find the tower height, correct to 1 decimal place.

examples.derivation: OT = 26 sin 30° = 13 m. Hence θ = arctan(13/20) ≈ 33.0239°, giving 33.0°.
The bearing difference is 90°. Equal elevation and depression angles give OP = 40 m and OQ = 40√3 m. PQ² = 1600 + 4800 = 6400, so PQ = 80 m exactly.
AC = √(9² + 12²) = 15 cm. The projection of AG is AC, so θ = arctan(7/15) ≈ 25.0169°, giving 25°.
OM = 20/2 = 10 cm. OM and TM are perpendicular to the planes' common edge AB. Their included angle is arctan(14/10) ≈ 54.4623°, giving 54.5°.
AC = 12√2 cm and OA = 6√2 cm. Since VO is perpendicular to the base, cos α = OA/VA = √2/2. Thus α = 45° exactly.
FP = √3h and FQ = h. The ground legs are perpendicular, so 3h² + h² = 100². The positive root gives h = 50 m exactly.
AF = h and BF = √3h. Northward AF is perpendicular to eastward AB, so 3h² = h² + 60². Hence h = 30√2 m ≈ 42.4264 m, giving 42.4 m.
The ground triangle is right-angled at O, with ∠OAB = 60°. AO = 80 cos 60° = 40 m. Then h = 40 tan 30° = 40/√3 m ≈ 23.0940 m, giving 23.1 m.
